title: Bi-Temporal Edge Invalidation in Dynamic Knowledge Graphs

claims.assertion: Facts in dynamic knowledge graphs must be modeled with bi-temporal valid_at and invalid_at timestamps to support non-destructive updates and historical state reconstruction

context: In conversational and agentic systems, real-world facts change over time (e.g. user location, project architecture, preferences). Overwriting graph edges or treating old facts as deletions destroys historical lineage and causes contradictory hallucinations in RAG retrieval.
distilled_learning: Represent relationship facts as EntityEdge models possessing both valid_at (when the fact became true) and invalid_at (when superseded or contradicted) timestamps. When an incoming episode provides contradictory assertions, update the existing edge's invalid_at to the episode timestamp rather than executing physical DELETE statements. Current truth queries filter for invalid_at IS NULL, while temporal queries can reconstruct the graph at any historical point in time.
